creator: Prathima WFPB
text:
This dessert is made with eyeball measurements. 

Base: Combine almond flour, cashews, walnuts, vanilla powder, and dates. Coarsely powder these ingredients (blend nuts coarsely before adding dates). Tap the mixture into a mold to create the base layer. This can be baked for a few minutes or used raw.

Mango Layer: Use frozen and fresh mango, and cashews. Create one layer of only mango puree, then top with chopped mango. Dates were not needed as the mango was ripe, but can be added if extra sweetness is desired.

Blueberry Layer: Use frozen blueberries, any nuts, and dates. Top with frozen blueberries.

The consistency of the layers is thick, so a divider is not needed for clean edges.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Cucumber, colored peppers, red onion, carrot, red cabbage, home-grown ash gourd, cauliflower, cilantro, coarsely crushed peanuts, salt, lime juice, white pepper powder, and chopped grapes.

Method: Chop all vegetables finely. Mix with coarsely crushed peanuts, salt, lime juice, and white pepper powder. Top with chopped grapes.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Method: Soak whole amaranth overnight. Boil it either in a pot for 25-30 minutes (stir constantly until thick) or in a pressure cooker for 10 minutes after the first whistle. Gurmeet preferred the taste of the pot-cooked version. 

Sweetener: Add blended dates and water, cardamom powder, allspice powder, and cinnamon. 

Serving: Top with fruits. Plant-based milk is optional.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients: Firm tofu (water drained and crumbled), spring onions, chopped red onion, garlic, chopped zucchini, baby spinach, goda masala, coriander+cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, green chili, mint leaves, cilantro, chopped tomato, snap peas, red radish. Any other vegetables like mushrooms, bell peppers, or broccoli can be added.

Method: Dry sauté the chopped onions and the spring onion bulb. Add the rest of the vegetables and spinach. Cook with a lid on for 3-4 minutes. Now add the crumbled tofu, tomatoes, mint leaves, and all the dry spice powders. Stir and cook until the water dries up a little bit. Garnish with cilantro.

recipe_name: Serving Tofu Bhurjee in Napa Cabbage Boats
creator: WFPB member
text: A cooking tip for Tofu Bhurjee is to serve it in napa cabbage leaves, which act as a 'boat.' The cool, crisp cabbage leaf adds a nice contrast and makes it fun to eat. Zucchini boats are also suggested as an alternative.

recipe_name: Homemade Soy Milk and Yogurt Discussion
creator: Group Member
text: A group member inquired about suitable soy milk brands in the US for making homemade soy yogurt and whether store-bought cashew yogurt could be used as a starter. Gunjan Sahni WFPB suggested that making soy milk at home is 'super easy.'

creator: Shilpa Mulberry WFPB
text:
Ingredients: A lot of curry leaves, cumin seeds, 1 tbsp peanuts, pumpkin seeds, white sesame seeds, brown sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, Dalia (roasted split chickpeas), and a pinch of black salt (to taste).

Method: Dry roast a generous amount of curry leaves. Grind them. Dry roast cumin seeds and grind them into a fine powder. Dry roast 1 tablespoon each of peanuts, pumpkin seeds, white sesame seeds, brown sesame seeds, black sesame seeds, sunflower seeds, and Dalia, then grind them coarsely. Mix all the ground ingredients together. Add a pinch of black salt to taste.

recipe_name: Enhancing Pistachio Cake to Tres Leches Style
creator: Gurmeet, Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text:
To make a pistachio cake sweeter or transform it into a Tres Leches style cake, pour sweetened plant-based milk over it, either while serving or by soaking the cake. If you prefer the pistachio cake alone, increase the sweetener quantity by 1.5 times for optimum sweetness.

Options for sweetened soy milk:
1. Add a thick paste of soaked cashews and raisins.
2. Add maple syrup and cashew butter.
3. Add date syrup and cashew butter.

Adding cashews to the milk is recommended for an enhanced dessert eating experience.

creator: Prathima WFPB, Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Prathima WFPB suggested creating a section on the group's website or a Google Doc for WFPB store-bought options, particularly for school snacks for kids. Gurmeet Singh Manku agreed, proposing that members contribute their findings to a Google Doc which could later be converted into articles.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Method: Soak a tablespoon of amaranth seeds in water for 24 hours, changing the water every 12 hours. After soaking, drain the water using a strainer and let the seeds sit in the strainer overnight, covered with a lid. Rinse again in the strainer and leave for another 10-12 hours. Finally, spread the seeds on a paper towel and cover lightly to allow air circulation. A sprouting jar can also be used. This method is an experiment to potentially grow them to microgreens.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB, Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text:
To give pav bhaji a buttery or cheesy taste using WFPB ingredients, prepare a spread:

Ingredients: Half a boiled potato, 10 soaked cashews, 1 tbsp nutritional yeast, 2-3 black peppercorns, a little lemon juice or vinegar, and optional salt.

Method: Pulse all ingredients nicely until a soft, butter-like consistency is achieved. Add 1-2 tablespoons of this spread on top of steaming hot pav bhaji just before serving. This spread is noted to taste more like cheese than butter and can also be used for vegan grilled cheese sandwiches. Alternatively, a little almond butter can be added to the final pav bhaji preparation.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
Ingredients: 2 cups dried chickpeas (do NOT use canned or cooked), 1 cup fresh parsley leaves (stems removed), 3/4 cup fresh cilantro, 1/2 cup fresh dill (stems removed), 1 medium white onion (quartered), 2-3 garlic cloves (peeled), 1 tsp ground black pepper, 1 tbsp ground cumin, 1 tbsp ground coriander, 1 tsp cayenne pepper, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 2-3 tbsp rice flour, salt to taste.

Method: Soak the chickpeas for 7-8 hours or overnight. In a food processor, run all ingredients except sesame seeds, rice flour, and salt until the mixture resembles medium breadcrumbs. Transfer to a bowl and add the sesame seeds, rice flour, and salt. Mix well. Form into flat 1.5-inch round discs. Air fry at the nugget setting at 350°F for 10 minutes per side. Serve with fresh babaghanouj, hummus, and salad.

creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam
text:
Ingredients: 1.5 cups Jowar, a handful of peanuts, 3-4 cups water, mustard seeds, jeera (cumin seeds), urad dal, green chili, onion (optional), red chili, curry leaves, vegetables (carrot, peas, corn, etc.), salt, sesame seeds, roasted peanuts, chopped coriander, lemon juice. Grated fresh coconut is optional for a satvic version, skip for WFPB.

Method:
1. Wash 1.5 cups of Jowar and soak overnight.
2. Discard the soaked water. Add a handful of peanuts and pressure cook the Jowar with 3-4 cups of water for 8-9 whistles (or use Instant Pot bean/chili mode). Check if Jowar can be mashed with two fingers; if not, cook for a couple more whistles.
3. In a pan, dry sauté mustard seeds, jeera, urad dal, green chili, onion (if using), red chili, and curry leaves.
4. Add chopped vegetables like carrot, peas, corn, etc., and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
5. Add the boiled Jowar (discarding any remaining water) and cook for another 3-4 minutes on medium flame with the lid on.
6. Sprinkle with sesame seeds, some roasted peanuts, chopped coriander, and lemon juice. Serve.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku's mom
text:
Ingredients: 3 cups small pieces of apple, beetroot, and whole plums (deseeded); 1 cup deseeded soaked dates; 2 cloves; 1/4 tsp ginger powder; 1/4 tsp cinnamon powder; 1 bay leaf; 1/2 tsp cardamom powder.

Method:
1. Boil or steam the apple, beetroot, and deseeded plums.
2. Grind or blend the cooked fruit and vegetable mixture with the deseeded soaked dates.
3. Cook the mixture in a pot with cloves, ginger powder, cinnamon powder, and bay leaf, stirring continuously until it reaches a thick consistency.
4. Turn off the flame and add cardamom powder. Mix well.
5. Cool the jam and serve with Whole Food Plant-Based bread, roti, paratha, puri, or cookies.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
Ingredients: 100 gms tofu, 40-50 gms besan (chickpea flour), black salt, a pinch of baking powder, 100-120 ml water.

Method: Blend all ingredients properly until smooth. Pour the mixture onto a very hot pan. Let it cook on medium to high flame for 1-2 minutes on both sides. Cover and cook until done.

recipe_name: Homemade Peanut Milk and Pulp Usage
creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam, Kusum WFPB
text: To make peanut milk, use a ratio of 1:4 (soaked peanuts to water), or 1:3. The peanut skin does not need to be peeled. A nut milk maker can be used for grinding and straining. The leftover peanut pulp is versatile and can be used to make crackers, laddoos (by adding dates), dried for later use, or incorporated into chapati dough.

creator: WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Oats, soy milk, blueberry, pomegranate, apple, banana, walnuts, almonds, flaxseed, chia seeds, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds.

Method: Combine all ingredients and soak overnight. Serve for breakfast.

recipe_name: Pineapple Oats Cake with Cream Topping
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text:
Cake Ingredients: 200 gms rolled oats, 100 gms pineapple chunks (instead of juice), 50 gms peanut butter, a pinch of salt, 1 tsp baking powder, 100-150 ml water (approx), 100 gms dates.

Cream Topping Ingredients: 1 boiled potato, a handful of cashews, 2 dates, some water, vanilla extract.

Method:
1. For the cake: Pulse all cake ingredients together until combined. 
2. Place thin pineapple slices at the bottom of a baking pan. Pour half of the batter over them. Add a second layer of pineapple slices, then cover with the remaining batter.
3. Bake at 180°C for 50 minutes. After 50 minutes, flip the cake over and bake for another 10 minutes.
4. For the cream topping: Blend the boiled potato, cashews, dates, some water, and vanilla extract until nicely smooth. This cream helps balance the sweetness of the cake if it's too sweet for your palate.

creator: Gurmeet
text:
Ingredients: Arbi (colocasia), green chili, chopped onions, cumin seeds, red chili powder, cumin+coriander powder, dry mango powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, cilantro.

Method: Pressure cook the arbi. Prepare an oil-free tempering by dry sautéing green chili, chopped onions, and cumin seeds. Add red chili powder, cumin+coriander powder, dry mango powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Add some water to the dry masalas to create a thick slurry before adding it to the sabzi. Garnish with cilantro. This is a quick preparation.

recipe_name: Cooking Tips for Cluster Beans (Guar Phali)
creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB, Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text:
Cluster beans (also known as Guar Phali, Guara Di phalli, chikkudukaya, chavlikai, gorikayi, kothavarakkai, or guvarsing) are rich in soluble fiber. Guar gum, a thickener used in many processed foods, comes from this bean.

Cooking Tips:
*   Gunjan Sahni WFPB cooks them with lots of garlic and green chili.
*   Shalini Other Lady WFPB strings the beans, steams them, and then sautés them with roasted besan (chickpea flour) and amchur powder (dry mango powder).

creator: Uma Venkataraman WFPB, WFPB member
text:
Ingredients: Silken tofu, curry leaves, green chilies, lemon juice, boiled vegetables (e.g., pushnikka/winter melon), optional celery stick, optional hemp, optional methi seeds, optional red chili, optional date, optional soy milk.

Method (Uma Venkataraman WFPB's version): Blend silken tofu, curry leaves, green chilies, and lemon juice. Add boiled vegetables (winter melon is a favorite and tastes better if soaked in the blended contents for a day). The mixture is not cooked, though leftovers can be warmed. Coconut is omitted for a WFPB version.

Variations (WFPB member's suggestions):
*   Add a celery stick and hemp as a replacement for coconut.
*   For a Kerala-style version, roast methi seeds and red chili, then blend with celery, hemp, soy milk, lemon juice, and a date. Serve with raw mango and winter melon.

recipe_name: Homemade Soy Milk and Yogurt Making Tips
creator: WFPB member
text:
Tips for making homemade soy milk and yogurt:
*   A NAMA juicer can make the process easier and less messy compared to using a blender and muslin cloth.
*   Soy milk needs boiling right after making it. It's best to use a portion of the freshly boiled milk to set yogurt immediately.
*   Soak organic soybeans (e.g., from Amazon) overnight, then give them a quick boil before milking them to reduce their strong flavor.
*   Alternatively, a Soyabella machine can be used, which boils, grinds, and strains all in one small machine.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB's daughter

Ingredients: Soy curd, pink guava, apple, other fruits for topping.

Method: Blend soy curd with pink guava and apple. Chill for some time to allow it to thicken. Serve with a few fruits as toppings.

While not extremely powerful, it is good for shakes, smoothies, and yogurt, and is easy enough for an 11-year-old to use without problems.

Leafy greens are almost always kept raw, but can sometimes be steamed (e.g., mustard greens). All other ingredients are used raw.

recipe_name: Navratri Fasting and Guided Fasting Resources
creator: Satvic Swetha Kogatam, Kusum WFPB, WFPB member, WFPB member
text: Discussion about Navratri fasting, with members expressing interest in raw plant-based diets, steamed meals (with exceptions), or 1-2 meals a day, as well as water fasting. Information was shared about guided fasting programs run by 'Lalit ji (LMK)' twice a year. These programs recommend eating approximately 500 calories once a day, provide sample meal pictures, and include educational posts on fasting, its effects on the body, and related topics (protein, carbs, etc.). A WhatsApp group link for LMK's health group for Navratri was also shared.
